output.brief: The rising rejects come from one combination: Arnholt resin dried in Press 5's dryer (D5), which is degraded. Press 5 with Arnholt rejects about 10%. Press 5 with Quillan, and Press 7 with either resin, stay under 1%. Arnholt resin arrives wetter, and D5 cannot dry it below the 0.20% limit. Quillan arrives drier, so it was tolerable. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects. The second-shift gap is only because all second-shift VX runs on Press 5. New and experienced operators have the same rates, so don't put the six on improvement plans. Dropping Arnholt isn't needed either. I'm about 90% sure. Next: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), confirm the dew point is back to -40, restore the original alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until then. Add a throat moisture check for every VX lot. Whether the north annex storage makes Arnholt wetter is unproven, because storage and supplier are confounded. Test that before paying for warehouse space. Tell the customer in the 8D that the cause is a dryer and resin interaction.
